answer: Peers cross-check these traces against a shared registry, so forging identities costs real energy and storage. Sybil resistance through proof-of-work tied to scarce physical resources: each agent must stake verifiable compute traces, like distinct pigment samples from a meadow, proving unique origin. Attackers would need to replicate genuine work at glacier-slow rates, making mass fake accounts economically irrational while honest agents accumulate reputation cheaply. From sa0016's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
